title: Tor vanishing under restriction along a flat base map
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $L$ be a $B$-module, $N$ an $A$-module, and $j\in\mathbb N$. If $\operatorname{Tor}^B_j(L,B\otimes_A N)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], then $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(\operatorname{Res}_A L,N)=0$. Every scalar action is induced by the given map $A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 069C, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, (3) implies (1), affine polynomial presentation; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/069C (read online)

proof.text: Let E and R be extension and restriction of scalars. Extension preserves projective objects by the adjunction because R preserves epimorphisms. Flatness gives finite-limit preservation of E followed by R (tensorLeft with B), so E preserves finite limits since R reflects them. Extension is a left adjoint and preserves finite colimits. It therefore maps a projective resolution P of N to a projective resolution Q of E(N).

source.place: Tag 069C, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, (3) implies (1), affine polynomial presentation; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/069C (read online)

proof.text: Construct E followed by tensorRight L followed by R naturally isomorphic to tensorRight R(L). Commute the B tensor factors, use AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange, restrict to A, and commute the A tensor factors. Naturality follows by tensor induction, with definitional equality on pure tensors. Lift this natural isomorphism to chain complexes and use exactness of R to commute it with homology. This identifies R(Tor over B at E(N), L) with Tor over A at N, R(L).

proof.text: Apply Tor symmetry over B to the zero object in the hypothesis. R maps it to a zero object; transfer across the homology comparison, and apply Tor symmetry over A to reach the required first-variable Tor object.
